# Artifact Keeper 1.11.0

A large release: about 340 changelog entries across about 220 merged pull requests since 1.10.0. The headline additions are hosted Arch Linux (pacman) and Bazel module repositories (#3343, #2858), a third repository visibility, `internal` (#3812), lifecycle policies that can be assigned to chosen repositories, combine conditions and reclaim a Remote's proxy cache (#3794, #4456, #3734), scan-on-proxy for Maven, Gradle, sbt, NuGet, Cargo and conda (#4100, #4102, #4101, #4585), private conda channels that pixi and rattler can use end to end (a package allowlist on virtual channels, #4576; CEP-16 sharded repodata on remote and virtual channels, #4577; tokens scoped to the one virtual channel consumers read, #4559; a configurable trust policy for CEP-27 attestations, #4556), Ed25519-signed webhooks verifiable against a public JWKS (#4401), image pulls from Kubernetes with a pod's ServiceAccount token (#1246), admin queues for quarantine holds (#4516), storage quotas enforced on every native format publish (#4422), a proxy download report that covers pull-through traffic (#3844), flat APT repositories such as `pkgs.k8s.io` through Debian Remotes (#4619), SMTP against a private CA with opportunistic STARTTLS (#4591), and distributed tracing that follows a request from the caller through the proxy to the upstream and the database (#4029, #4434, #4455). The rest is mostly security and correctness work on proxies, virtual repositories, formats and storage, including six security advisories fixed in one batch (#4588) and the bug batches found while building the private conda channel walkthrough. This page groups the highlights; the `## [1.11.0]` section of `CHANGELOG.md` has every entry.

1.11.0 also contains every fix shipped in 1.10.1 and 1.10.2, listed again under their sections below as 1.10.0 did for 1.9.1. If you are upgrading from 1.10.2, these 14 entries are already deployed: the repository-management token scopes (#3831), the webhook read gate (#3901), the four token-restriction fixes (#4219, #4225, #4226, #4228), the conda native-PUT scan (#4159), the Composer metadata deadlock (#4170) and wasmtime 36.0.16 (#4332), all from 1.10.2; and from 1.10.1 the OSV dependency-scanning fixes (#4079, #4080, #4081), the repository format string (#4083) and the hex `JWT_SECRET` check (#4211). wasmtime 36.0.17 (#4361) and the conda repodata deadlock fix (#4145) are new in 1.11.0.

**Upgrading from 1.10.2 runs 58 migrations; from 1.10.0 or 1.10.1, 60** (222 to 289, excluding the numbers that were never used; 235 and 237 shipped in 1.10.2). One of them, **233, requires stopping every old backend replica before it runs**; see the first section. Eight rewrite or backfill existing rows (228, 268, 270, 271, 276, 278, 284 and 288), six build indexes `CONCURRENTLY` (230, 266, 272, 274, 281 and 283), and 279 briefly takes an exclusive lock on the proxy-cache tables; see "Operations and migrations".

## Read this first: stop all replicas before migration 233

**Lifecycle policies are now scoped by explicit repository assignments, and an older binary misreads the new scope as "every repository"** (#3794, migration 233). A policy now carries `applies_to_all` plus a list of assigned repositories. Older binaries treat any policy that has no single `repository_id` as global. The migration itself maps every existing policy to a shape an old binary still reads correctly, but as soon as a 1.11.0 replica creates a dormant or multi-repository policy, or a repository is deleted (its single-repository policies become dormant instead of being deleted), an old replica or lifecycle scheduler still running would read that policy as global and could delete artifacts across the whole instance.

- **Scale the backend to zero (or otherwise stop every old pod and scheduler) before upgrading. Do not do a rolling or mixed-version deploy.** Helm upgrades are rolling by default.
- Downgrading to 1.10.x after 233 is unsafe unless policy scopes are first reconciled by hand.
- Two API changes come with it. Creating a policy without `repository_id` now creates a dormant policy that deletes nothing, not a global one: CLI, Terraform and other clients that relied on the old default must send `applies_to_all: true`. Deleting a repository no longer deletes its single-repository policies; it removes the assignment and leaves the policy dormant.

The migration itself preserves behaviour: a policy with a null `repository_id` becomes `applies_to_all = true`, and a single-repository policy gets one assignment.

## Read this second: requests that are now refused

- **Storage quotas now apply to every native format publish: `507`. Check usage against quotas before upgrading** (#4422). Until now only the generic upload API, chunked uploads and `npm publish` checked `quota_bytes`. Maven, Cargo, Helm, Go, Docker and every other native publish counted toward the repository and project totals but was never refused, so a repository or project could grow past its cap. **A repository or project that is already over its quota refuses every publish that adds bytes after the upgrade**, until usage drops below the cap or the quota is raised. A publish that adds no bytes is always admitted: a re-push of a blob the repository already holds, or an overwrite with identical or smaller content. Most formats, Cargo, Git LFS and Swift included, answer the generic `507 {"code":"QUOTA_EXCEEDED",...}` body rather than a format-native error; `docker push` answers the registry envelope (`507`, code `DENIED`), Protobuf (BSR) a Connect `resource_exhausted` error with status 507, and an Incus upload refused after its `202` marks the upload session `failed`. Docker usage now counts each layer once, and migration 288 recomputes stored usage (#4483, #4545; see the third section), so a capped Docker repository no longer refuses pushes well before its real bytes reach the cap. A manifest whose descriptors declare a negative or absurd size is rejected with `400 MANIFEST_INVALID`. Promotions, migration imports, peer replication and proxy-cache fills are still not checked against the target's quota (#4546).
- **Origin policies now gate what a Remote serves from its proxy cache or upstream, metadata included: `403`. Review global origin policies before upgrading** (#4506). A scan policy's `origin` predicates (`allowed_upstreams`, `denied_upstreams`, `allowed_repositories`, `denied_repositories`, `allowed_kinds`) were evaluated only against an `artifacts` row's recorded origin, and a Remote fetch writes a proxy-cache row and no `artifacts` row, so an upstream deny policy never stopped a proxied download and `allowed_kinds` naming `proxy` could never be satisfied (#4161). Content a Remote serves now carries the origin `{"kind": "proxy", "repository_key": <remote key>, "upstream_url": <its configured upstream>}`, and the policies that apply to the Remote, its own and the global ones, are evaluated against it before the cache is read or the upstream is contacted. A refused download answers `403 Artifact download is blocked by the repository's scan policy`, for entries cached before the policy was attached and on the presigned-redirect fast path too, and a virtual repository does not serve the refused content from that member either. **A global policy with `allowed_upstreams` that does not list a Remote's upstream, or with `allowed_kinds` that does not include `proxy` (for example one that allows only hosted kinds), now refuses every download from every Remote.**
- **Six security advisories are fixed in one batch, and four of them refuse requests that used to pass** (#4588). Eight REST mutation endpoints now check the caller's action on the repository instead of stopping at a token scope, the tenant gate or authentication alone (GHSA-mvmh-g8wm-r3cp): linking or unlinking a release target needs the repository `admin` action, rejecting a staged artifact needs the promotion capability, repository label writes need `write`, email subscriptions need `admin` (listing them exposed recipient addresses, and creating one made the instance mail arbitrary addresses), image builds need `write` when `AK_IMAGE_BUILD_ADMIN_ONLY=false`, a build can be changed only by its creator or an administrator (migration 285 records the creator; builds from before the upgrade are administrator-only), peer connection probes are admin-only, and proxy-scan rescans need `write`. Refusals are `403`, or `404` where the caller cannot read the repository; a `developer` member keeps label writes, image builds and rescans. `PUT /api/v1/repositories/{key}/security` now needs the `write:repositories` token scope, as the sibling configuration endpoints already did, so a `read:artifacts` token held by a repository admin can no longer turn scanning off (GHSA-gvhj-8vg9-358g). A download ticket carries the repository restriction of the credential that minted it (migration 286), minting one needs `read:artifacts`, and tickets minted before the upgrade are refused; they live seconds to minutes, so a client only mints again (GHSA-2mfv-xg68-gq4p). The same change repairs ticket redemption, which had been failing for every ticket and broke the web UI's `?ticket=` downloads and the Terraform provider mirror's archive URLs (#3588). An image-build package spec containing a line break or another control character answers `400`; a pip requirement such as `foo[a\nRUN ...]` used to add its own instruction to the generated Containerfile, past `AK_IMAGE_BUILD_ALLOW_RUN=false` (GHSA-59mx-6fq9-pp9p). The other two advisories, stalled uploads and upstream credentials, are in the next bullet and in the third section.
- **Stalled uploads are cut off with `408`, a principal is capped at 64 uploads in flight with `429`, and an upload the server could not receive in full is no longer called an invalid package** (#4588, GHSA-9f9r-c4w8-rjv9; #4609). A user with write access to one Git LFS repository could open 512 uploads, send one byte on each and hold every global request slot, so `/health` and `/ready` answered `503` and the orchestrator restarted the replica. An upload body that delivers fewer than `UPLOAD_MIN_PROGRESS_BYTES` (default 16384) during `UPLOAD_PROGRESS_WINDOW_SECS` (default 60) spent waiting for data is aborted with `408` (a progress floor, not an idle timeout, so trickling one byte at a time does not keep a request open); a principal (an authenticated user, or a client address when anonymous) may have at most `UPLOAD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT_PER_PRINCIPAL` (default 64) uploads in flight on the native-format routes, the repository artifact routes and `/api/v1/uploads`, and the next one gets `429` with `Retry-After`; the health and readiness probes bypass the global concurrency limit; and Git LFS objects stream to the upload scratch disk while being hashed instead of being buffered in memory. `0` turns each limit off. Separately, the archive-parsing publish routes (conda, RubyGems, npm, Cargo, Composer, Hex, VS Code, Go modules, Alpine, pacman, CRAN, RPM) answered every receive failure with `400 Failed to buffer the request body` and buffered each body at about twice its size, so two concurrent 1.5 GB conda uploads OOM-killed a 4 GiB replica. They now receive the body into one buffer of its declared size, charged to a process-wide `UPLOAD_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES` (default half the cgroup memory limit), and check it against `Content-Length` before parsing: a body cut short is `408` with code `incomplete_body`, a full budget is `503` with `Retry-After`, a full scratch or storage disk is `507` instead of a bare `500`. **A `400` from these routes now always means the complete package arrived and is itself invalid.** PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Terraform, Swift, Chef and Pub spool through helpers that apply the same rules. See `docs/operations/upload-scratch-disk.md`.
- **A virtual repository whose member fails answers `502` naming the member instead of a smaller index, and a member that does not answer within 20 seconds is such a failure** (#4192, #4555, #4508). The merge behind Helm `index.yaml`, CRAN `PACKAGES` / `PACKAGES.gz`, Hex `/names` and `/versions`, Bazel module metadata and conda `repodata.json` / `channeldata.json` logged a member it could not fetch or parse and served the rest with `200`, so a client concluded that member's packages did not exist, or resolved a name present in two members to the lower-priority one. By default any such member now fails the request with `502` and the cause. A virtual with `virtual_metadata_partial: true` (`PATCH /api/v1/repositories/{key}`) instead gets the merge of the healthy members, with `X-AK-Partial-Members` naming the missing ones, `Cache-Control: no-store` and a `Warning: 199`. Each failure counts in `ak_virtual_member_metadata_failures_total{format,virtual_repo,member,reason}`. A member that answers `404` publishes no such document and is not a failure: a conda member without a subdir or without `channeldata.json` contributes nothing (#4555, #4601), and members the caller may not read are left out without being reported. Each Remote member's metadata fetch is also bounded by `AK_VIRTUAL_MEMBER_METADATA_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 20) on the Maven `maven-metadata.xml` and `.meta/prefixes.txt` merges, the shared first-hit metadata walk and the merged indexes above: a member whose upstream blackholes connections used to stall every metadata miss for the upstream client's 60-second timeout, longer than most reverse proxies wait, so clients saw `504` and builds crawled; it is now a `502` after 20 seconds (`reason="timeout"`, counted in `ak_virtual_member_metadata_timeouts_total{member}`). Artifact downloads are not bounded by it. A Hex Remote member whose upstream is `repo.hex.pm` serves the signed protobuf registry rather than the JSON `/names` and `/versions` merge, so, like a `404`, it contributes nothing and does not fail the merge (#4629). A database failure while authorizing a virtual's members (a pool timeout under load) answers a retryable `503 POOL_EXHAUSTED` instead of `404 Virtual repository has no accessible members`, which Gradle cached as missing until its cache was cleared (#4308).
- **Scan-on-proxy is enforced on conda and `conda_native` Remotes and virtual channels** (#4585, part of #4097). A Remote with `scan_on_proxy` on runs `.conda` and `.tar.bz2` downloads through the same inline gate as npm, PyPI, Cargo, Maven, NuGet, OCI and VS Code: `fail_open` serves with `X-AK-Scan: pending` and scans in the background, `fail_closed` scans inline and answers `423` when inconclusive, `record_only` serves with `X-AK-Scan: recorded`, and a blocked package answers `403 {"error": "scan_blocked", ...}`. A virtual channel scans each Remote member under the stricter of its own and the member's policy, the `/t/<token>/` URL forms are covered, a `.sigs` attestation sidecar is refused when its package's verdict blocks, and repodata, channeldata and shards are not gated. `GET /api/v1/formats` reports both formats as `enforced`. On a conda repository that scans on proxy the generic download route refuses proxied files with `403 scan_on_proxy_route_required` (#4442), and a package path containing `?`, `#`, `;`, `\`, a control character, a stray `%` or a space is `400`. **Grading changed so that `fail_closed` is usable against conda-forge** (#4594, #4600): no bundled scanner catalogs a conda package as a conda component, so a scan that completed over the unpacked archive and cataloged nothing (`tzdata`, `ca-certificates`), or cataloged the vendored upstream name (`libzlib-1.3.1` as `zlib 1.3.1`), was inconclusive, which answered `423` for most of conda-forge under `fail_closed` and served `pending` forever under `fail_open`. For conda such a scan is now graded on its findings, `clean` with none and `vulnerable` with any, and the verdict records `components_cataloged` (migration 287; `0` means graded on contents only, `null` a verdict from before 1.11.0). A scan that could not run, or a package whose `info/index.json` disagrees with its file name, is still withheld. Other formats keep the catalog identity check.
- **A Conan revision is published by its manifest, and a `conanmanifest.txt` that arrives before the files it needs answers `409`** (#4329). The Conan client uploads a revision's files one at a time, archives first and manifest last, and carries on after a file fails. When a 3.5 GB `conan_package.tgz` was cut off by the router-wide request timeout, `conaninfo.txt` and the manifest still landed, so consumers got `corrupted in the server, it doesn't contain a conan_package.t file` and re-running the upload skipped the package as already there. Files uploaded before the manifest are stored but not listed by `/latest`, `/revisions`, `/search` or `/files`; the manifest is accepted only once `conaninfo.txt` and `conan_package.t*` (for a binary) or `conanfile.py` plus the export archives it names (for a recipe) are stored, and is otherwise refused with `409` and nothing stored. Conan file transfers are now exempt from `GLOBAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS` like OCI blobs and LFS objects, and a body shorter than its `Content-Length` is `408` with nothing stored.
- **Hex publish without a usable `CHECKSUM` member answers `422`** (#2904). Such a tarball used to be stored and then made every `/packages/{name}` read answer 500. `mix hex.build` always writes the member, so only hand-built tarballs are affected.
- **`POST /api/v1/signing/keys` with `key_type = ed25519` answers `400`** (#1326). That combination never produced an Ed25519 key: it stored an RSA keypair labelled `ed25519`, which could not sign Debian or RPM metadata. Ask for `key_type = gpg` with `algorithm = ed25519`, which now generates a real v4 EdDSA OpenPGP key. Existing `ed25519` rows keep loading.
- **A CI OIDC credential can no longer mint an API token: `403`** (#4314). `POST /api/v1/profile/access-tokens`, `POST /api/v1/auth/tokens` and `POST /api/v1/repositories/{key}/tokens` refuse a caller that is a CI OIDC service account, whichever provider type issued its credential. Before, a short-lived pipeline or `kubernetes` credential could mint a `read:artifacts` token that, under the default token policy, never expires. A pipeline that did this must exchange a fresh CI token per job instead; an administrator can still issue a token for a CI account through the admin endpoints. CI OIDC exchanges also refuse an assertion whose `nbf` is more than 60 seconds in the future with `401` (#4511).
- **Creating or updating a repository as public while guest access is disabled answers `400`** (#3855) instead of silently storing it as private. Terraform and other clients that send `is_public: true` on a guest-disabled instance must stop doing so.
- **A lifecycle policy that cannot reclaim anything in a Remote repository answers `422` when it is assigned there** (#3734): `max_versions`, `tag_pattern_*`, `size_quota_bytes`, `exclude` lists and `min_keep` match artifact versions that proxy-cache entries do not have. OCI Remotes are exempt. Policies already assigned keep running.
- **Scan-on-proxy now enforces for Maven, Gradle, sbt, NuGet, Chocolatey, PowerShell and Cargo Remotes that already had it enabled** (#4100, #4102, #4101), and for the VS Code legacy download route (#4098). A vulnerable package answers `403 scan_blocked`, and under `fail_closed` an unscannable one answers `423`. These pulls were served unscanned before, so gates that were never exercised can start blocking. `GET /api/v1/formats` reports which formats enforce (#4099); `docs/security/scan-on-proxy.md` has the matrix (#4114).
- **The generic download route refuses proxied files of an enforced format while the repository scans on proxy: `403 scan_on_proxy_route_required`** (#4442). `GET /api/v1/repositories/{key}/download/*path` (also `/general/{key}/*path`, and the web UI's download button) streamed a Remote's cached or upstream bytes without the scan gate that the format routes apply to the same bytes. When a Remote of an enforced format has `scan_on_proxy` on, this route now answers `403` with a `handler` field naming the format route to use instead, under every `proxy_scan_action` including `record_only`, for every path and for `HEAD`. A Virtual repository refuses the same way, on this route and on `GET /api/v1/repositories/{key}/artifacts/*path`, when a readable Remote member scans; a hosted member's own file is still served. Clients that downloaded such files through the generic route must switch to the format route.
- **Ambiguous proxied paths answer `400`, and an unreadable scan setting answers `503`** (#4513, a slice of #4365). On the npm, PyPI, Cargo and VS Code routes and the generic route's Remote arm, a client path containing `?`, `#`, `;`, `\`, a control character or a stray `%` is refused before any upstream request (Maven, sbt and NuGet already did this), so a query can no longer be smuggled to the upstream. A database error reading `scan_on_proxy` now answers a retryable `503` on every enforced format instead of streaming unscanned, and a VS Code Remote that scans on proxy answers `404` for any gallery asset type outside the display-metadata allowlist.
- **Lifecycle regexes are PostgreSQL regular expressions, validated by PostgreSQL, and `\b` / `\B` are refused** (#4461, #4502, #4504). Creating or updating a policy answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` for a pattern PostgreSQL rejects or cannot compile within 2 seconds, for `\b` / `\B` (in PostgreSQL `\b` is a backspace, so `\bstable\b` protected nothing; use `\y` / `\Y`), for back-references, for a pattern over 512 bytes and for more than 64 exclusions. Stored policies are not changed: startup logs one WARN per offending policy, a preview lists the problems in `errors`, and a live or scheduled run refuses, with `400` naming the field, a policy whose exclusion would fail open or whose scope or `tag_pattern_delete` pattern uses `\b`. Fix such a policy with `PATCH /api/v1/admin/lifecycle/{id}`.
- **Webhook event names are validated: `400`** (#4419). `POST /api/v1/webhooks` accepted any string in `events`, so `artifact.uploaded` was stored and never fired (deliveries match `artifact_uploaded`). Unknown names are now refused with the accepted list. Webhooks already stored with an unknown name are unchanged and still never fire; recreate them.
- **Generic, chunked and multipart uploads refuse Remote (`405`) and Virtual (`400`) repositories** (#4420), as the native format routes already did. A user with write access could otherwise plant an artifact in a Remote that shadowed its upstream. A chunked session opened against such a repository before the upgrade can no longer be completed.
- **`PATCH /api/v1/repositories/{key}` applies `upstream_url`** (#4467) instead of answering `200` and ignoring it, and **answers `409` when the change moves a Remote with upstream-auth credentials to another origin**, so the stored credentials are never sent to a host they were not configured for. Remove the credentials, change the URL, then configure new ones.
- **Known-malicious packages are graded `Critical`** (#3013). OSV `MAL-*` advisories usually carry no severity and used to default to `Medium`, below a typical `max_severity = high` gate. They are now classed `malicious` and graded `Critical`, so a gate can start blocking packages it used to pass.
- **A multipart publish over `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` answers `413`, not `400`** (#3936), and **completing a chunked upload onto an occupied immutable path answers `409`** instead of replacing the artifact (#3924).
- **Smaller refusals.** A conda upload whose subdir disagrees with the package's own `info/index.json` answers `400` naming both values, and a `POST` without `X-Conda-Subdir` files the package under its own subdir instead of `noarch` (#4555). A Terraform module upload that is not a ZIP or a gzip-compressed tar answers `400`, because neither `terraform` nor `tofu` can install anything else (#4590). A second scan policy with the same name on the same repository answers `409`, compared case-insensitively; a re-run setup script used to stack identical policies (#4558). A virtual conda merge that cannot start within `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_QUEUE_SECS` (default 60) answers `503` with `Retry-After` (#4608; see Formats). An anonymous OCI manifest `PUT` answers `401` with the push challenge instead of `500`, and the body is read only after the caller is authorized (#4568). On the SMTP test endpoint an invalid recipient answers `400` instead of `500`, and a failed delivery answers `502` with the reason (#4591; see Operations).

## Read this third: behaviour that changes without an error

- **Docker Hub credentials need a trusted token realm** (#3591). Since GHSA-78h6-3wp8-2542 a Remote only sends its upstream credentials to a Bearer realm on the upstream's own origin, and Docker Hub issues tokens from `auth.docker.io`. The new per-Remote `oci_trusted_bearer_realms` list names the extra origins that may receive them. Nothing is trusted by default, Docker Hub included: **a credentialed Docker Hub Remote must add `"oci_trusted_bearer_realms": ["https://auth.docker.io"]`** to pull private images or use its account rate limits. Without it, pulls fall back to anonymous tokens. Split-host GitLab registries need the same. See `docs/oci-trusted-bearer-realms.md`.
- **A Remote's upstream credentials go only to its configured upstream's origin** (#4588, GHSA-24rf-2gv2-j47c). Index metadata can name download locations by absolute URL (a PyPI simple-index `href`, a Helm `index.yaml` `urls` entry, the Cargo `config.json` `dl` template, a Composer `dist.url`, a Terraform `download_url`), and the shared fetchers attached the Remote's Basic or Bearer credentials to whatever URL they were given, so a compromised index could collect them, over plain HTTP if it named an `http://` URL, triggered by any client that could request the download. Credentials are now attached only when the request URL has the same scheme, host and port as `upstream_url` or `index_upstream_url`; any other URL is still fetched, without them, with a sampled `security` warning. **A credentialed Remote whose upstream serves files from a different host than its index, and needs the same credentials there, now gets `401` or `403` from that host.** For a Cargo registry with split hosts, set `index_upstream_url` to the index and `upstream_url` to the download host, so both are configured origins. OCI realms (`oci_trusted_bearer_realms`) are unchanged.
- **A token scoped to a virtual repository now reads the virtual's members through it** (#4559). A repository token minted on a virtual, or a user token whose `repo_selector` names it, was refused every member, so a virtual conda channel answered `404 Virtual repository has no accessible members` and no per-repository consumer token could be issued for the one channel URL consumers use. Such a token now reads the members on requests routed through the virtual: the format endpoints (`/conda/<virtual>/...`, `/pypi/<virtual>/simple/...`), the `/t/<token>/` forms, and the virtual's member listing, artifact listing, download and storage total. Each member is still checked against the token owner's grants, a request to a member's own URL with such a token is still `404` (which keeps a per-virtual conda allowlist from being bypassed through the member), and deploying through a virtual still needs the scope to name the hosted member.
- **Maven unique snapshots are overwritable again** (#4476), reversing part of #3839. A build that deploys the same attached artifact twice in one `mvn deploy` uploads the same timestamped file twice; up to 1.8.0 the second upload replaced the first, and since 1.10.0 it answered `409` and failed the build. Snapshots are documented as overwritable, so every file under a `-SNAPSHOT` version directory, unique or not, is republished in place again. Release coordinates still answer `409`, a version that merely contains the token (`1.0-SNAPSHOT-rc1`) is still a release, and the proxy cache's classification of unique snapshots is unchanged.
- **Version comparison honours epochs, so curation rule matches change for epoch-bearing versions** (#4507). `version_compare` left a Debian/RPM `N:` or PEP 440 `N!` epoch glued to the first segment, so `1:2.0-1` sorted below `10.0-1`. Epochs are now compared numerically first, a missing epoch counting as 0. A block rule `< 10.0` no longer matches `1:2.0-1`, and an allow rule `>= 10.0` now does. Hex, NuGet and packages API listings order such versions the same way.
- **Severity counts use one definition, so repository scores and grades can change on upgrade** (#4338). The Overview dashboard, the security dashboard, the per-repository scores and the artifact view disagreed on the same data: the tiles counted finding rows, so one CVE in two packages, or from two scanners, counted twice; repository scores were recomputed only after a scan, so acknowledging a finding moved the tiles but not the repository row; and the Overview counted every CVE ever recorded, acknowledged ones included. All of them now count, per artifact, the latest completed scan of each type, one vulnerability per advisory at its highest reported severity, open ones in the severity buckets and acknowledged ones separately. Acknowledging a finding recomputes its repository's score, a CVE the latest scans no longer report is marked `fixed` in the artifact's history, and `total_findings` on a repository score is now its open vulnerabilities.
- **Docker/OCI usage counts each layer once, and migration 288 recomputes stored usage** (#4483, #4545). An OCI manifest's `artifacts` row records the image size, and those bytes were counted again through `oci_blobs`, once more per extra tag, so a repository holding 1.10 GB of blobs showed 4.69 GB and a capped Docker repository refused pushes early. Usage and the quota ledger now leave out the `oci-manifests/` rows, as the storage panel already did (#3286); the manifest documents themselves (a few KB each) are no longer counted. `artifacts.size_bytes` keeps the image size, so tag listings, the packages catalog and the UI are unchanged. **Expect `storage_used_bytes` on Docker repositories to drop after the upgrade.** A Remote download larger than the repository quota no longer leaves a 0-byte "cached" entry in the catalogue; it is still counted as a download (#4551).
- **Uploads into a staging repository are recorded as `hosted`, and promotion copies the package's metadata and reports every gate rule** (#4557, #4152, #4556). The origin derivation stamped a staging upload `virtual`, so a promoted copy showed as "stored in a virtual repository" and an `allowed_kinds: ["hosted"]` predicate refused it; migration 284 re-stamps those rows. Promotion also inserted no `artifact_metadata` row, so a promoted conda package was served with empty `depends`, no `md5` and no attestation; the document is now copied. `POST .../promote`, single and bulk, adds `gate_results: [{"rule", "passed", "reason"}]` listing every rule the promotion was evaluated against, passed predicates included (`Policy 'release-gate' [conda.license]: license 'mit' is allowed`), next to the existing `policy_violations`. A verified CEP-27 attestation on a hosted conda package now satisfies `min_attestation_state: verified` and the promotion `require_signature` gate, which only read the curation record and the signing key's audit entries before.
- **Lifecycle policies reclaim a Remote's proxy cache only when explicitly assigned to that Remote** (#3734). `max_age_days` and `no_downloads_days` now evict proxy-cache entries, but global (`applies_to_all`) policies never reach a Remote cache, which may hold the only copy of content that is gone upstream. A global run says so in `proxy_cache.skipped_reason`. Run a preview before assigning one: `max_age_days` evicts by cache age, however often an entry is used.
- **A virtual repository's `storage_used_bytes` is now `0`; its members' total moves to `member_storage_used_bytes`** (#4423). Since #2785 a virtual repository reported the sum of its members as its own `storage_used_bytes` (list, detail, create and `PATCH` responses), so any total that added up repositories counted those bytes twice. The member total, still limited to the members the caller can see, is now in the new `member_storage_used_bytes` field (`null` for other repository types), and project quota rollups skip virtual repositories. Totals that sum `storage_used_bytes` need no change and are now correct. The create response reports the member total too, instead of `0` until the next `GET` (#4505). **Dashboards and clients that show a virtual repository's size, including the web UI and CLI until their follow-up releases (artifact-keeper-web#958, artifact-keeper-cli#181), show `0` until they read the new field.**
- **Cache TTLs: higher ceiling, and lowering one takes effect at once** (#2667, #3832). The per-Remote TTL override can now go up to ten years (315360000 seconds), which stops revalidation of mutable paths. Lowering a TTL now applies to entries already cached instead of waiting out each entry's original expiry, and a `304` revalidation refreshes `cached_at`. The web UI's TTL input still has the old maximum (artifact-keeper-web).
- **`AK_GUEST_ACCESS_ENABLED`, when set, overrides the new runtime toggle** (#867). Guest access can now be switched at runtime through `PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings/system`. An explicit `true`/`false`/`1`/`0` in the environment still wins, as an offline break-glass. To hand an instance that runs with `false` over to the admin setting without reopening anonymous access, `PATCH` `false` first, then remove the variable.
- **Webhooks v2** (#4401). A webhook's new `signing_mode` (`hmac`, the default; `asymmetric`; `both`) adds a `v2=<kid>:<sig>` Ed25519 signature verifiable against `GET /api/v1/webhooks/jwks`. Existing webhooks stay `hmac` and their headers are byte-identical. `asymmetric` and `both` need `AK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY` set; if that key changes after the signing key exists, asymmetric deliveries go out without `v2=` until an administrator retires the key by hand (the SQL is in the CHANGELOG entry). Key rotation follows in a later release.
- **`ak_http_request_duration_seconds` is a histogram now, so its `quantile` series are gone** (#4434). Panels and alerts that select `{quantile="0.99"}` must use `histogram_quantile()` over the `_bucket` series, which also makes the percentile aggregatable across replicas. Each label set exports 16 series instead of 9.
- **An OCI image deleted by digest stays deleted after a restart** (#4450, #4465). The startup repair that re-registers manifests imported by the migration tooling treated any live untagged manifest row as a never-indexed import, so an image pushed only by tag (for example by `skopeo copy --all`) and deleted by digest on an older release, or by a not-yet-upgraded replica during the rollout, came back on the first restart after the upgrade. The repair now also requires `artifacts.origin` to record a migration import (`kind = migration`, stamped by the worker since #4050 and by migration 270 for older imports), so a row written by `docker push` is never repaired. One case remains: a migrated image pushed only by tag and deleted by digest on an older release still looks like an unindexed import; delete it again after the upgrade. A delete by digest is also scoped to the image named in the request (#4466), and `GET` / `HEAD` by digest on a hosted repository resolve under that image name too (#4525): a digest deleted under `xa` answers `404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN` there and keeps resolving under `xb`, which still tags it.
- **Upstream credentials embedded in a Remote's `upstream_url` are no longer returned by the API** (#4452), **and the copies kept elsewhere are stripped** (#4463): migration 271 removes the `user:password@` part from `artifacts.origin` and the proxy-cache catalogue, and triggers keep it out from then on. The Remote's own `upstream_url` still holds the credentials, because the proxy authenticates with them. Rotate any secret that was embedded in a Remote's URL and move it to the encrypted upstream-auth fields; `PATCH upstream_url` now applies (#4467). Origin policies' `allowed_upstreams` / `denied_upstreams` now match artifacts proxied through such a Remote, which they never did. A Remote URL containing whitespace or control characters is refused with `400`.
- **Content imported by the Artifactory / Nexus migration tooling is re-labelled `migration`** (#4153). The origin backfill (228) recorded it as `hosted`; migration 270 re-stamps a row only when one completed migration item for the same repository unambiguously claims its path and SHA-256. Anything ambiguous stays `hosted`. Compare `SELECT count(*) FROM artifacts WHERE origin->>'kind' = 'migration'` before and after if you want to see the effect.
- **An OCI Remote whose upstream refuses the credentials it sent answers `502 DENIED`, not `404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN`** (#4453, #4518). This covers a refusal from the token service and from the registry's manifest request, and logs a rate-limited `security` warning naming the (redacted) upstream. It applies only when credentials were actually sent (#4527): an anonymous refusal, including one from an untrusted cross-origin realm, still answers `404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN`, because Docker Hub answers `401` for an image that does not exist.
- **The bundles API is a preview** (#4400, #2464): it describes and validates the bundle format, but `POST /api/v1/bundles/exports` and `/imports` answer `501` until the export and import steps land. **Remote and virtual pacman repositories are not supported yet** (#4407).
- **Presigned download redirects need `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` / `AZURE_STORAGE_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` when clients reach the object store through a different host than the backend** (#4417). Redirects used the backend's own storage endpoint, so with an in-cluster `S3_ENDPOINT` every redirected download from outside failed. Set the new variable to the address clients use (do not enable `PRESIGNED_DOWNLOADS_ENABLED` without it in that topology); a malformed value stops the backend at startup, and its credentials are redacted from the error (#4503). Unset, nothing changes. See `docs/operations/presigned-downloads.md`.
- **The npm age gate keeps a package's own `latest`** (#4432) instead of pointing it at the newest allowed version, prereleases included (`npm install typescript` resolved to a nightly). When the gate blocks `latest`, it moves to the newest allowed release at or below it.
- **The admin download report includes proxy serves, and `artifact_id` can be `null`** (#4539, #3844). `GET /api/v1/admin/downloads` and its `by-ip` / `by-user` variants now list proxy pull-through serves next to hosted downloads. Each row carries `source` (`hosted` or `proxy`), `repository_id` and `path`, and `artifact_id` is `null` on a proxy row. **A client generated from the 1.10 spec that types `artifact_id` as required fails to read a page that contains a proxy row**; pass `source=hosted` to get the previous hosted-only listing. `GET /api/v1/admin/stats` `total_downloads` now counts hosted and proxy downloads, with the new `proxy_download_count` as its breakdown (the old figure is `total_downloads - proxy_download_count`). The `/api/v1/analytics` snapshots are unchanged and stay hosted-only. Cache eviction no longer deletes proxy download history, so `proxy_download_statistics` now grows until its repository is deleted (retention is #4541).
- **Cross-replica single-flight waits for the leader: keep `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS` below your ingress read timeout** (#4532, #4013). With `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_ADVISORY_LOCKS_ENABLED=true`, a replica that loses the lock for a cold streamed object now blocks until the leader has published it to the cache, for at most `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 65), and only then fetches on its own. nginx-ingress reads for 60 seconds by default, so with both defaults an ingress can cut off a waiting client before the backend falls back; set the wait below the ingress timeout. Each waiting replica holds one database connection per cold object, outside the pool, capped by `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_MAX_LOCK_WAITERS` (default 32 per replica; past the cap a replica fetches at once); count them when sizing `DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS` times replicas against PostgreSQL's `max_connections`. If the leading replica's node is lost mid-download, the waiting replicas take over after about 30 seconds, once PostgreSQL's TCP keepalives on the lock session reap it. With the flag off, the default, nothing changes.
- **npm tarballs on S3, GCS and Azure go to per-repository keys** (#4293). Tarballs were written to the flat key `npm/{package}/{version}/{file}`, which every repository on a shared object-storage namespace shares, so publishing the same version to a second npm repository was refused with `409 ... already owned by another repository`. New tarballs on a cloud backend are written under `npm/{repository_id}/{package}/{version}/{file}`, the scheme Maven already uses (#2624). Existing tarballs stay where they are and keep serving from the key their artifact row records; filesystem storage and `STORAGE_KEY_SCHEME=flat` keep the flat key.

## Known issues

Reproduced on 1.10.2 and unchanged in this release, so none of these is a regression; they are tracked in #4593 for 1.11.1. Each one refuses access rather than granting it.

- **A `global` permission grant gives no repository access.** `POST /api/v1/permissions` accepts `target_type: "global"` (for example with `actions: ["admin"]`), but repository reads consult only `repository` and `project` grants, so a user, group or service account whose only grant is global gets `404` on every private repository. Grant on each repository, or on its project, instead.
- **A service account's API token does not grant access on its own.** The repositories chosen on the token narrow what the token may reach; the service account still needs its own permission on a private repository. A service account with `is_admin` acts as an administrator only through a token carrying the `admin` or `*` scope.
- **`/api/v1/repositories/{key}/download/...` answers an anonymous request for a private repository with `404` and no `WWW-Authenticate` challenge**, so a client that sends credentials only after a challenge (wget, Maven by default) never authenticates; an API token is also not accepted as the Basic password on `/api/v1`. Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or `X-Api-Key: <token>`, or use the format route (`/general/{key}/...`, `/maven/{key}/...`), which challenges and accepts `<user>:<token>` Basic credentials.
- **GNU wget 1.25 aborts on the `401` from a private format route**, because it selects the `Cargo` challenge the response also offers. Use `wget --auth-no-challenge --user=<user> --password=<token>`, or `curl -u <user>:<token>`.

## Security

- **Advisories.** Six GitHub security advisories are fixed together (#4588): eight REST mutation endpoints that did not check the caller's action on the repository (GHSA-mvmh-g8wm-r3cp), the repository scan-configuration endpoint accepting a token without `write:repositories` (GHSA-gvhj-8vg9-358g), download tickets rebuilt from the user account instead of the minting credential's restriction (GHSA-2mfv-xg68-gq4p), a line break in an image-build pip requirement adding its own `RUN` instruction past `AK_IMAGE_BUILD_ALLOW_RUN=false` (GHSA-59mx-6fq9-pp9p), stalled uploads holding every global request slot so that health probes answered `503` (GHSA-9f9r-c4w8-rjv9), and upstream credentials sent to any host an index named (GHSA-24rf-2gv2-j47c). The second and third sections say what each one changes for clients.
- **Tokens and access control.** A personal token created with a `repo_selector` is confined to it (#4219); a repository-restricted token can no longer mint an unrestricted one (#4225); a restriction no longer fails open on an unreadable selector or a misspelled field (#4226); a token whose repositories were all deleted no longer becomes unrestricted (#4228); webhook fetch-by-id needs the same grant as the listing (#3901). All five shipped in 1.10.2. Artifact label writes need the repository `write` action (#4193), bulk promotion applies the quality gate and the CVE and licence policy per item (#3979), and the CI OIDC exchange no longer merges principals across issuers or reactivates a deactivated account (#4032). The OCI `/v2/token` exchange is rate limited (#4020) and now has its own per-user bucket, `RATE_LIMIT_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_PER_WINDOW` (default 300 per `RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_WINDOW_SECS`), instead of spending the ten-per-fifteen-minutes login budget, which a `podman push` followed by `cosign sign` and `cosign verify` exhausted (#4558). Promotion history and the release-target endpoint now take the repository read gate, answering `404` to a caller who cannot read the repository and blanking a counterpart repository the caller cannot see (#4418, #4473). A repository the caller cannot read now answers exactly like one that does not exist, `{"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"Repository not found"}`: the two 404s had different bodies, so an anonymous caller could tell that a private repository exists (#4498). Git LFS batch download actions carry the caller's `Authorization` header and are marked `authenticated` only when they do, so `git lfs pull` from a private repository no longer retries a 401 forever, and batch responses are `Cache-Control: no-store` (#4570). CI OIDC credentials can no longer mint API tokens (#4314), and assertions are checked for `nbf` (#4511). A `kubernetes` CI OIDC provider mints pull-only, non-renewable credentials (#1246). A token scoped to a virtual repository reads its members through it (#4559; see the third section).
- **Leaks.** Upstream credentials embedded in `upstream_url` are redacted from every API response, audit record and log line that carried them (#4452) and stripped from the origin records and proxy-cache catalogue that stored them (#4463, migration 271). A rejected `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` / `AZURE_STORAGE_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` no longer logs its credentials (#4503). The bearer token in a conda token-channel URL (`/conda/t/<token>/...` and rattler's `/t/<token>/conda/...`) was written in clear to the request span's `uri`; that segment is now `[REDACTED]` (#4565). **Rotate any token used through these URLs if your logs or trace backend may have been read by someone who should not hold it.** Conda channel responses to authenticated requests are `Cache-Control: private` instead of `public`, so a shared cache in front of the registry cannot store a private channel's index, or a virtual's index as merged for one caller, and serve it to the next requester (#4555). LDAP login no longer reveals through its timing whether a username exists (#3505), and the detailed health payload no longer echoes the raw storage error (#3907).
- **Content that should not have been served.** npm and Maven virtual repositories no longer serve a hosted member's artifact that the member's scan policy blocks (#4286), RPM virtual repodata lists only the members the caller may read (#4346), and the VS Code legacy download route is scan-gated (#4098). The generic download and artifact routes no longer serve proxied files around scan-on-proxy (#4442), an unreadable scan setting fails closed (#4513), and generic uploads can no longer plant files in Remote or Virtual repositories (#4420). Origin policies now gate what a Remote serves from its cache or upstream (#4506; see the second section), and conda Remotes and virtual channels are scan-gated (#4585). A virtual conda channel no longer lets a remote member shadow a package name a hosted member owns, the dependency-confusion guard npm, PyPI, Cargo, RubyGems and Hex already had: ownership is read from every member regardless of the caller's access, and a database error fails the request instead of merging unguarded (#4555). Its sharded endpoints follow the repository's read access, which a private hosted channel used to answer anonymously (#4577). Hash-based scan reuse copies only from a scan that actually ran, so a verdict can no longer outlive the scan behind it by chaining copies (#4425), and the reuse index covers only this instance's own scans (#4426).
- **Content that should have been served.** A layer shared with an image blocked by scan policy no longer blocks every clean image that uses it (#4380, the p0 of this release). On an OCI Remote with scan-on-proxy, one blocked image made `GET /v2/<name>/blobs/<digest>` answer `403` for any layer it shared, under every image name in the repository, so clean images sharing a base layer with it could not be pulled. A blob carries no image identity, so it is now refused only when no image in the repository that references it would be served by the manifest gate; the blocked image is still refused at its manifest, and its config and own layers by digest. The dashboard's `policy_violations_blocked`, previously always `0`, now counts proxied content the gate refuses on formats that run it, plus hosted artifacts in the `rejected` quarantine state (#4380, #4582).
- **Tracing input.** Once `RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` is set, inbound W3C trace context is adopted only from peers inside it, so other clients can no longer force or suppress sampling (#4195). With the list empty, the default, the header is still accepted from every client, and startup warns when the configured sampler is one a client can force.
- **Dependencies and images.** The WASM plugin runtime moves to wasmtime 36.0.17 for RUSTSEC-2026-0321, -0322 and -0323 (#4361, new in 1.11.0), on top of 36.0.16 for RUSTSEC-2026-0314 and -0316 (#4332, already in 1.10.2). The scanner adapter is 1.4.1, rebuilt on hardened trivy 0.74.0-r4 with its Go toolchain floor at go1.27.2 (#3579), and the backend image's bundled `grype` and `buildctl` are rebuilt from source on go1.27.2 with `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 (#3698); together these clear Go's October security release (CVE-2026-78667, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-97031) from the image gate, which had blocked every `main` build from 2026-10-10. `grype --version` and `buildctl --version` report the same versions as before. The stock `docker-compose.yml` publishes Postgres and OpenSearch on `127.0.0.1` only and no longer publishes Trivy or OpenSCAP; a default `docker compose up -d` on a host with a routable address used to expose Postgres with its fixed login and OpenSearch with its security plugin disabled (#4480). CEP-27 conda attestations are verified when `CONDA_ATTESTATION_REQUIRE_VERIFIED` is set (#4155), and the trust policy is now configurable, including key-based Sigstore bundles for on-premises CI (#4556; see Formats).

## Proxy and virtual repositories

- **Filters and isolation.** A Remote can restrict which paths it requests upstream with include and exclude patterns, and a virtual no longer waits on a member whose filter excludes the path (#4399). npm virtual repositories can isolate hosted package names from upstream (#3767), and virtual conda channels now do the same for names a hosted member owns (#4555) and can restrict what remote members contribute to an allowlist (#4576; see Formats). Docker Hub and split-host registries can authenticate through trusted realms (#3591).
- **Member failures and deadlines.** A member that fails to fetch or parse, or does not answer within `AK_VIRTUAL_MEMBER_METADATA_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 20), fails the merge with `502` naming it, or is reported in `X-AK-Partial-Members` when the virtual sets `virtual_metadata_partial`; a `404` from a member is not a failure (#4192, #4555, #4508, #4601). A database error while authorizing members is a retryable `503`, not a `404` that Gradle caches (#4308). See the second section.
- **Caching.** TTL ceiling and immediate TTL lowering (#2667, #3832); Go module versions are cached instead of revalidated every five minutes (#4120); GitHub release-by-tag lookups are cached for seven days (#3658); a request arriving during a refill no longer duplicates the upstream fetch (#4298); remote Debian pool downloads no longer list the whole proxy cache (#4315). An npm Remote's cached packuments no longer appear in its cached-artifact listing or the proxy-scans view as if they were packages (about 1.9 MB of JSON that could be "downloaded" but not deleted); they stay in the cache and in storage accounting (#4305). A Remote download larger than the repository quota no longer leaves a 0-byte catalogue entry (#4551). A Cargo pull-through asks the upstream for the crate name exactly as the client spelled it, so `Inflector` and other crates with an uppercase canonical name download again (crates.io stopped serving other spellings in 2023); the cache key stays lowercase (#4339). A NuGet Remote lowercases the whole flat-container path, id, version and file name, so a mixed-case request reaches the upstream and the same cache entry (#4528).
- **Debian flat repositories** (#4619). Remotes and virtuals mirror flat APT repositories (`deb <uri> /`) such as Kubernetes' `pkgs.k8s.io` and the openSUSE Build Service, which only speak the layout without `dists/<suite>`. `InRelease`, `Release` and `Release.gpg` pass through byte-for-byte so apt keeps verifying the publisher's key, each index is checked against the signed `Release` before it is served, a package is cached only when it matches the SHA-256 its `Packages` records, and flat-layout packages are cached as immutable. Point apt at `deb [signed-by=<publisher key>] <base>/debian/<repo>/ /`. `debian.flat_repository = true` declares a Remote flat; left unset, both layouts are served.
- **Virtual correctness.** Nested virtual members resolve (#3840); npm virtuals no longer fail `npm install` with EINTEGRITY when a hosted member shadows a remote one (#3955) and walk members concurrently (#4240); Cargo virtuals use each member's own download template (#3952) and shadow only the exact local `name@version` (#3953); NuGet serves both protocol surfaces across all members (#4126), and a V2 member whose upstream answers `index.json` with an error is no longer dropped from the virtual (#4327). `ansible-galaxy collection install` resolves collections through a virtual Ansible repository: the Galaxy metadata routes read the members in priority order instead of the virtual's own, always empty, artifact set, and every `href` and `download_url` points back at the virtual (#4379). Terraform modules install through a virtual: `/download` answers `204` with `X-Terraform-Get` pointing at the virtual's own `/archive`, as a hosted member does, and `/versions` lists the union of the members' versions, and on a Remote the upstream's, neither of which was listed before (#4598). Creating a virtual reports its members' storage total at once (#4505).
- **Scan-on-proxy.** New enforcement for Maven, Gradle, sbt, NuGet and Cargo (#4100, #4102, #4101) and for conda (#4585, with grading on contents for packages the scanner cannot catalog, #4594, #4600; see the second section); a `record_only` action that records findings without blocking pulls (#3645); quarantine holds stop virtual walks (#4098); the generic download route defers to the format routes (#4442). A shared OCI layer is refused only when no clean image needs it (#4380). The first slice of canonical proxy paths (#4513, part of #4365) derives each request's proxy-cache key and scan decision from one normalized path for Maven, sbt, NuGet, npm, PyPI, Cargo and VS Code; cache keys for well-formed paths are unchanged, so no warm entry is orphaned.
- **Single-flight across replicas.** With `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_ADVISORY_LOCKS_ENABLED=true`, requests for a cold streamed object coalesce in-process first, only one request per replica contends for the cluster lock, and a replica that loses waits for the leader's cache publish and serves its waiting requests from the cache (#4532, the first slice of #4013). On 3 replicas, 200 concurrent GETs of a cold 256 MiB object made **one** upstream fetch and returned 200 correct bodies; before, the same storm made 94 to 100 fetches, many answered `502`. The worst case, a leader still downloading when the wait times out, is one fetch per replica. The wait timeout and connection settings are in the third section.
- **Download statistics for proxied traffic** (#3844). A virtual download answered by a Remote member is counted once, under that member's repository and path, and members that were probed but lost are not counted (#4535). Proxy download history survives cache eviction, so per-path counts continue across a re-cache (#4539, migrations 277 to 283), and the admin download report and `/admin/stats` `total_downloads` include proxy serves (#4539; see the third section). npm tarballs served directly from a Remote without scan-on-proxy are counted again; that path recorded nothing, while the same tarball through a virtual was counted (#4341). An all-proxy deployment no longer reports zero downloads.

## Formats

- **New.** Hosted pacman repositories with on-demand `.db`/`.files` and detached signatures (#3343); Bazel module registry (Bzlmod) repositories (#2858); GitHub release mirroring through `github`, `mise` and `aqua` formats (#3656); a hosted VS Code repository served through the gallery protocol, and virtual galleries (#3959, #3962); flat APT repositories through Debian Remotes (#4619; see the previous section).
- **Signing.** Ed25519 OpenPGP keys (#1326), an overlap window in which both the old and the new key sign Debian and RPM metadata after a rotation (#1329), and a startup warning, with optional automatic replacement, for keys that cannot sign the metadata they are bound to (#1331).
- **RPM, Maven, Debian and others.** Hosted RPM repositories publish dependency metadata (#3801), serve metadata at a configured directory depth (#4216) and can prune curated snapshots (#4406). Maven: uploads commit atomically (#3587), `.meta/prefixes.txt` no longer breaks Maven 4 (#4367), virtual downloads count (#4267) and unique snapshots are overwritable again (#4476; see the third section). `.safetensors` uploads expose tensor structure (#4402); chunked uploads of Incus images and Debian packages get native metadata (#4403); RubyGems remote specs no longer come back empty (#4280). RPM curation sync reads zstd, xz and bzip2 compressed `primary.xml` (the createrepo_c default on Fedora and EL9 mirrors, which used to sync as an empty repository) and reports a sync that ingests nothing as failed (#4427); a Fedora Everything primary needs `MAX_INGEST_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES` raised above its 128 MiB default. Two concurrent publishes of one RPM curation version no longer interleave repodata; the second gets `409` (#4421). Rotating a signing key created without a `repository_id` now repoints the repositories bound to it (#4416).
- **Conan.** Conan v2 answers 404 for missing items (#3887). `conan remove` works against a local repository: the four DELETE routes the Conan 2 client uses (a recipe, a recipe revision with its binaries, every binary of a revision, one package revision) are served, need the `delete:artifacts` scope and the repository `delete` permission, and soft-delete like every other delete path (#4333). Package search returns each binary's `conaninfo.txt`, so `conan list -p "os=Linux"` and `conan download -p` filter instead of matching nothing (#4334). Recipe and package `/latest` report the revision's stored time, the same one `/revisions` shows, instead of the clock at request time (#4335). Uploads are atomic and published by their manifest (#4329; see the second section).
- **Terraform.** `terraform init` and `tofu init` install hosted modules (#4590): `/download` advertised no archive type, so the client fetched the archive as an HTML page and failed on its bytes. The type (ZIP or gzip-compressed tar) is detected at upload, recorded, and advertised as `.../archive?archive=zip` or `?archive=tar.gz`; modules uploaded before this release have theirs read from the stored bytes. Remote Terraform repositories answer `/download` with the same `204` + `X-Terraform-Get` pointing at their own `/archive`, which streams the upstream archive through the proxy cache; before, the upstream `204` was relayed as an empty `200`. Virtual repositories do the same (#4598). A new native test runs the real CLI against hosted and proxied modules.
- **npm.** A package mixing numeric and hash prerelease versions (`confusing-browser-globals`) no longer panics its packument through an age-gated repository; the curation comparator behind Hex, NuGet and package version listings had the same cycle (#4431). The age gate keeps the package's own `latest` (#4432). Tarballs on cloud storage go to per-repository keys (#4293; see the third section).
- **OCI.** A delete by digest is scoped to the named image (#4466), and so is a `GET` / `HEAD` by digest on a hosted repository (#4525); deleting the last tag of a tag-only image drops its `oci_manifests` record (#4449); upstream credential refusals answer `502 DENIED` (#4453, #4518, #4527). Promoting an image now makes it pullable from the target repository (#4578): promotion copied only the tag's `artifacts` row and the top-level manifest, so a pull from the target answered `MANIFEST_UNKNOWN` while the API reported `promoted: true`, and `promotion_only` Docker repositories had no way to receive a working image. The single, bulk and approval paths now walk the image index, its child manifests and every config and layer blob, copy what the target lacks and record the tag, manifest references and `oci_blobs` rows in one transaction; a source image with a missing blob fails the promotion instead of producing an empty tag. An anonymous manifest `PUT` answers `401` with the push challenge before any body is read, so `crane`'s retry after a token exchange works and an unauthenticated client can no longer make the server buffer a manifest (#4568). Usage counts each layer once (#4483, #4545, migration 288), the upgrade repair re-registers only migrated images (#4465) and an over-quota proxied download leaves no placeholder (#4551); all three are in the third section.
- **pacman.** File lists move out of package metadata into their own table (migration 276), so `pacman -Sy` no longer makes PostgreSQL read every package's file list, and the `.files` database is rendered once per repository state (#4424).
- **Conda: private channels for pixi and rattler.** Channels accept rattler's token URL layout, `/t/<TOKEN>/conda/<repo>/...`, which `pixi auth login --conda-token` produces, beside the `.condarc` layout `/conda/t/<TOKEN>/<repo>/...` (#4555); the `Authorization` header remains the recommended form, since a token in a URL can end up in logs and lockfiles. The `unknown` subdir, which pixi requests when no platform is given, is served as an empty index instead of `400`, which aborted the whole query (#4555). Every hosted record carries a server-set `indexed_timestamp` (CEP-47), the moment the package entered the channel, taken from the artifact's `created_at`, so a client cooldown such as pixi's `exclude-newer` cannot be defeated by a publisher's clock; a package promoted into a channel is indexed at its promotion time there (#4555). `repodata.json` no longer carries `info.base_url`, and shard indexes carry `base_url: "./"` and `shards_base_url: "./shards/"`, the values rattler's own indexer writes, so packages resolve against the URL that served the document (#4580): with the usual enterprise `[mirrors]` rewrite of `conda-forge` to the registry, rattler resolved the old host-relative `base_url` against `conda.anaconda.org` and every `pixi exec` and `rattler-build` environment failed with `404`, a proxy in front of the registry sent clients to the registry's path on the proxy's host, and a token channel lost its token on every package URL. A token scoped to the one virtual channel consumers read now works (#4559; see the third section). The content-analysis work (#4033 and follow-ups) identifies what is inside a package, maps conda dependencies to PyPI advisories (#4042, #4089), records provenance and publisher identity (#4049, #4050), and can withdraw a single package with a CEP-6 notice (#4059); `conda_native` packages now get the same scanner-component dedup against the PyPI distribution they vendor as `conda` packages do (#4254).
- **Conda: virtual channels.** A package allowlist on a virtual channel restricts what its remote members contribute (#4576). `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/v1/repositories/{key}/allowlist` (repository admin; audited as `REPOSITORY_ALLOWLIST_CHANGED`) takes `{ "name", "version", "subdirs" }` entries: `name` an exact name or a `*`/`?` glob, `version` an optional conda version spec in conda ordering (`2.2.*`, `>=2,<3`, `1.0|1.1`), `subdirs` an optional platform restriction. When `enabled`, a remote record the list does not admit is left out of `repodata.json` and `channeldata.json` and answers `404` on download without contacting the upstream, so a client reports the package as not found instead of failing at download. Hosted members are never filtered, an enabled empty list admits nothing from remotes, and merged documents report the records left out in `X-AK-Allowlist-Dropped`. Remote members are fetched as `repodata.json.zst`, then `.bz2`, then `.json`, through the budgeted proxy path under `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MEMBER_MAX_BYTES` (default 128 MiB compressed) and `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MEMBER_MAX_DECODED_BYTES` (default 1 GiB), one member at a time, and merged as raw JSON on a blocking thread; before, every request parsed a few hundred MiB of conda-forge JSON per member into a tree with no ceiling (#4555, #4180). Hosted members merge first, then remote members in priority order, first writer wins per filename, and once a hosted member has published a name no remote member contributes under it in any subdir (#4555). A member's missing subdir or missing `channeldata.json` contributes nothing instead of failing the merge (#4555, #4601).
- **Conda: concurrent solves no longer exhaust memory** (#4608). Every request for a virtual channel's `repodata.json`, `channeldata.json` or shard index ran its own merge, outside the buffered-metadata budget: 20 concurrent `repodata.json.zst` requests took the backend to 20.8 GB, and at a 12 GiB limit it was OOM-killed. Requests for the same merged document now share one merge, and its encoded result is kept for `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_CACHE_TTL_SECS` (default 300, `0` disables) under one `ETag`, so revalidation answers `304`; kept documents are capped by `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` (default 1 GiB). A kept merge is reused only while the caller-visible member set, the hosted records, the owned names, the allowlist and each remote member's fresh proxy-cache entry are unchanged, and a merge with a failed member is never kept. At most `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MAX_CONCURRENT_MERGES` merges run at once (default: the buffered-metadata budget divided by the member ceilings, at least 2), each reserving its fetch buffer, decoded documents, working set and output from `AK_PROXY_METADATA_BUDGET_BYTES` before it starts, and a merge that cannot start within `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_QUEUE_SECS` (default 60) answers `503` with `Retry-After`. The same 20 requests now peak at 0.7 GB, and a 40-way cold-cache `pixi install` stampede completes under an 8 GiB limit with the backend below 1 GB. Metrics: `ak_conda_virtual_merge_inflight`, `ak_conda_virtual_merge_cache_hits_total`, `ak_conda_virtual_merge_cache_misses_total`, `ak_conda_virtual_merge_rejected_total` and `ak_conda_virtual_merge_bytes_reserved`; sizing and restart alerting are in `docs/operations/conda-virtual-merge-memory.md`.
- **Conda: CEP-16 sharded repodata on remote and virtual channels** (#4577). Sharded repodata was served for hosted channels only, so pixi fell back to the monolithic index on every solve; for the private-channel pattern, where consumers only read a virtual, that meant a 74 MB merged `linux-64/repodata.json.zst` per solve instead of a half-megabyte shard index and a few hundred small shards. A Remote proxies its upstream's shard index, rewritten so shards resolve against the registry, and each shard by address through the proxy cache as immutable; a shard that does not hash to its address is `502`, never served or cached. A virtual merges its members' indexes under the same rules as `repodata.json`: hosted shards first, a name a hosted member owns never taken from a remote, the allowlist applied per name. Two limits follow from a shard being admitted whole: where two remote members publish the same name, the sharded view carries the first member's records only, and a name the allowlist admits only under a version constraint is left out of the sharded view and stays in `repodata.json`. Hosted shard indexes and shards are written with msgpack `bin` digests and without a `Content-Encoding: zstd` header, which invited HTTP clients to strip the zstd frame before the CEP-16 reader saw it (#4555, the encoding half of #4173; materialising shards at write time is still open). A virtual serves every shard its merged index lists (#4607): admission used to be decided by decoding the shard and requiring one admitted record, so conda-forge's empty `noarch` shard for `cuda-nvcc_linux-64` (90 bytes, one `removed` entry) answered `404`, which pixi and rattler treat as fatal, and every cold sharded solve through a virtual whose closure touched pytorch or jax failed. Admission now comes from the merged index itself: a shard refused by policy is `404`, and a listed shard the member cannot produce is `502` naming the member, never a `404` that tells the client the package does not exist. Ceilings: one upstream shard may decode to 16 MiB instead of 8 (conda 26.7 rejects anything larger, and the largest conda-forge shard decodes to 6.2 MB), and an upstream shard index past the 8 MiB metadata tier is read again under its own 64 MiB ceiling, so conda-pypi's 28.6 MB noarch index is served instead of `502`; past 64 MiB the Remote answers `404`, as does a virtual over it, and clients fall back to `repodata.json` (#4612).
- **Conda: CEP-27 attestations** (#4556). Upload verification accepted only keyless Sigstore bundles whose Fulcio certificate named the GitHub Actions issuer, which an organisation's own CI cannot produce. `CONDA_ATTESTATION_ISSUERS` (default the GitHub Actions issuer, so nothing changes unset), `CONDA_ATTESTATION_IDENTITIES` (certificate identity patterns, `*` wildcard; empty accepts any identity the issuer vouches for) and `CONDA_ATTESTATION_PUBLIC_KEYS` (PEM file paths or inline PEM, each optionally `name=`-prefixed) now define the policy. A bundle from `cosign attest-blob --key ... --tlog-upload=false` verifies when its DSSE signature verifies under a configured key (ECDSA, Ed25519 or RSA), its in-toto subject matches the SHA-256 of the stored bytes and its statement passes the CEP-27 policy; no Fulcio certificate or transparency log is consulted, so the configured key is the trust anchor. Statement v1, as CEP-27 specifies, and the v0.1 `cosign` still emits are both accepted. The stored `attestation_verification` says how it verified (`method`, `identity`, `issuer`, `statement_type`, `key_fingerprint`), and `GET /api/v1/attestations/policy` returns the policy, public material only, to any authenticated caller. Attestations are append-only, served as CEP-50 sidecars at `{file}.sigs` and, immutably, `{file}.sigs.{sha256}`, advertised in every repodata record and shard as `attestations_sha256`, and readable by anyone who can read the package (a public channel used to demand credentials for them); virtual channels serve the sidecar from the member that holds the package, and Remotes proxy the upstream's. A verified attestation now satisfies `min_attestation_state` and the promotion `require_signature` gate (see the third section).

## Lifecycle, storage and uploads

- **Lifecycle.** Explicit assignment (#3794), composite conditions and tag or version patterns (#4456), newest-N retention under an age rule and path-prefix scope (#2024), and proxy-cache reclamation for Remotes (#3734). Every pattern is validated by PostgreSQL, which runs it (#4461); a stored pattern that cannot compile is reported by a preview and refused by a live run with `400` instead of `500` (#4502, #4504).
- **Trash and repair.** `GC_TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS` keeps soft-deleted artifacts restorable by an admin for that many days; the default `0` keeps today's behaviour (#2072). Storage scrub detects, and from a verified copy repairs, corrupt content-addressed objects (#3910). Admins can register artifacts that exist in storage with no database row (#1570).
- **Uploads.** Receive failures are reported as what they are, `408`, `503` or `507`, under a process-wide memory budget, `UPLOAD_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES` (#4609); stalled uploads are cut off by a progress floor and a principal is capped at 64 in flight (#4588); Conan revisions are published atomically by their manifest (#4329); all three are in the second section. Incus chunked image uploads work behind more than one replica (#4302, migration 289): each chunk is staged as an object on the repository's storage backend and recorded on the session in commit order, so any replica can take any chunk, and the completing replica copies them into its own staging file. The completion reads the whole image back from storage once more, each chunk costs one extra object write, and a session started before the upgrade keeps the local-file path and still needs session affinity to finish.
- **Object storage.** Raw `PUT` and multipart uploads into S3, GCS and Azure no longer spool to local disk (#3916, #4404); OCI blob pulls can be served by a presigned-URL redirect (#2894); quality checks read the repository's configured backend (#3736); chunked uploads work behind several replicas (#3918) and clean up after themselves (#3922). `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` and `AZURE_STORAGE_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` point presigned redirects at the address clients use (#4417). npm tarballs on cloud backends go to per-repository keys, so the same version can be published to more than one npm repository (#4293). A virtual repository's size moves to `member_storage_used_bytes` (#4423, #4505), and Docker usage counts each layer once (#4483, #4545); both are in the third section.
- **Projects.** Project admins manage their own membership and repositories (#2473), and project storage quotas are enforced across the project's repositories (#2474). Repository and project quotas now apply to every native format publish, not only generic uploads and npm (#4422; see the second section).
- **Promotion and curation.** Promotion copies the artifact's format metadata and reports every gate rule in `gate_results`, for single and bulk promotions alike (#4556, #4557); staging uploads are recorded as `hosted` (#4557, migration 284); curation version constraints honour epochs (#4507). All are in the third section.

## Observability

The backend joins the caller's trace (#4029), adopts it only from trusted proxies once configured (#4195), and its sampler is configurable through `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` (#4029). Upstream requests are `CLIENT` spans that carry the trace onward (#4434, #4455), the request span records the route, status, repository and cache outcome, and authentication, virtual-resolution and proxy-fetch phases appear as their own spans (#4455). With export configured, SQL statements can appear as `CLIENT` spans; SQL text is never exported (#4455). Request-scoped stdout log lines now show these spans too. `ak_http_request_duration_seconds` is a Prometheus histogram instead of a summary (#4434; see the third section). OTLP `http/protobuf` export works (#3833), and the gRPC and metrics listeners can bind a specific IP (#2161).

`/readyz` now reports its dependencies (#4610). It keeps meaning "this replica can serve artifacts" (database reachable, migrations applied), but its body always carries a `dependencies` object (`opensearch`, `storage`, `scanner`, `ldap`, each `healthy`, `unhealthy` or `not_configured`, with whether it is `required`), probed concurrently with a 2-second deadline each, and a `failing` list when not ready; probe error text appears only with `EXPOSE_DETAILED_HEALTH=true`. `READYZ_REQUIRE_SEARCH=true` (default false) makes an unhealthy or unconfigured OpenSearch a `503` naming `opensearch`. See `docs/operations/health-probes.md`. New counters: `ak_virtual_member_metadata_failures_total` and `ak_virtual_member_metadata_timeouts_total` (#4192, #4508) and the `ak_conda_virtual_merge_*` family (#4608). Severity counts on every dashboard now share one definition (#4338), and `policy_violations_blocked` counts what the proxy scan gate actually refuses (#4380, #4582); both are in the third section.

## Operations and migrations

**58 migrations** run on start-up from 1.10.2 (222 to 289 as present on disk, 60 files, less 235 and 237), **60** from 1.10.0 or 1.10.1, which also apply 235 and 237. Most are additive. The ones to plan for:

- **233** (#3794) needs every old replica stopped first; see the first section.
- **228** backfills `artifacts.origin` for existing rows in resumable batches outside a transaction (#4050). It runs once, on the upgrade that applies it, and its time grows with the number of artifacts.
- **268** creates the `oci_manifests` table (#4433); a background task started at boot then records manifests pushed before the upgrade, reading each body from storage. Nothing reads the table yet in 1.11.0, so the backfill is not on any request path. A 1.10.x replica writes no row for its pushes, which is one more reason to stop every old replica before upgrading (migration 233 requires it anyway); reconciling the table is part of the later release that starts reading it.
- **227 to 230** are the origin work: 227 adds the column and its trigger, 228 the backfill above, 229 validates the constraint (`VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`, which takes no write lock and builds no index), and 230 builds the upstream index `CONCURRENTLY`.
- **270, 271 and 284** rewrite origin rows after the 228 backfill: 270 re-stamps content imported by the migration tooling as `migration` (#4153), 271 strips credentials from stored upstream URLs in `artifacts.origin` and `proxy_cache_artifacts` (#4463), and 284 re-stamps staging uploads, and the copies promoted from them, from `virtual` to `hosted` (#4557). Each runs in 5000-row batches with a 5-second `lock_timeout` per batch and retries, takes no table lock on `artifacts`, and admits exactly its own rewrite through the 227 immutability trigger only for its duration, then restores the strict trigger. 270 logs its counts as `NOTICE` lines under `sqlx::postgres::notice` at INFO.
- **276** creates `pacman_file_lists` and moves existing pacman file lists out of `artifact_metadata` in resumable batches of 100 rows (#4424). It is forward-only: rolling back past it leaves `.files` with empty file lists.
- **277 to 283** (#4539) key `proxy_download_statistics` on the Remote repository and path it was served from, so download history survives cache eviction. 277 adds the columns, a `NOT VALID` foreign key and an insert trigger that keys rows written by a not-yet-upgraded replica; 278 backfills existing rows in resumable 5000-row batches with a per-batch `lock_timeout`, outside a transaction and without a table lock; 279 takes `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` on `proxy_cache_artifacts` and `proxy_download_statistics` for a catalogue-only change (no scan; proxy serves wait at most its 5-second `lock_timeout`) and relaxes the foreign key to the cache to `ON DELETE SET NULL`; 280 to 283 build the history and by-IP indexes `CONCURRENTLY`. Each proxy serve now writes two more columns and two more index entries, plus a foreign-key check against `repositories`.
