- **288** replaces the usage-ledger trigger function so that OCI manifest rows no longer count toward `hosted_bytes`, and re-seeds `hosted_bytes` for every repository that holds such rows (#4483, #4545). The trigger itself is unchanged, so no trigger DDL runs and no table lock is taken on `artifacts`. The background reconciler and `POST /api/v1/admin/storage/ledger/backfill` apply the same rule.
- **285, 286, 287 and 289** are catalogue-only column additions: `builds.created_by` (#4588; builds from before it are administrator-only to change), `download_tickets.scope_recorded` and `allowed_repo_ids` (#4588; tickets minted before it are refused at redemption), `proxy_scan_results.components_cataloged` (#4594) and `incus_upload_sessions.staged_parts` (#4302; `NULL` marks a session started by an earlier version, which keeps its local-file path).
- **Concurrent index builds.** 266 and 272 build the quarantine-hold indexes behind the new admin queues (#4516), 281 and 283 build the proxy download history indexes (#4539), and 273 to 275 rebuild the scan-reuse index online under a new name, `idx_scan_results_dedup_local`, then drop the old one (#4426). The 273 to 275 build reads `scan_results` twice, waits for transactions already open, and needs disk space for both indexes until 275 runs. **New in 1.11.0, start-up repairs an interrupted concurrent build**: if a build listed in `CONCURRENT_INDEX_MIGRATIONS` (266, 272, 274, 281, 283) was cut off, for example by a lock timeout behind a long transaction, the next start drops the INVALID leftover before migrating, so the retry rebuilds it and the old index is never dropped while the new one is unusable. See `docs/operations/online-migrations.md`.
- **257** adds `key_source` and `static_jwks` to `ci_oidc_providers` with defaults that keep existing providers unchanged (#1246). Rolling back makes a `kubernetes` provider act as `generic` (unrestricted, renewable tokens), so disable those before any rollback.

**New settings in this release.** Uploads: `UPLOAD_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES`, `UPLOAD_PROGRESS_WINDOW_SECS`, `UPLOAD_MIN_PROGRESS_BYTES`, `UPLOAD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT_PER_PRINCIPAL` (#4609, #4588; second section). Virtual repositories: `AK_VIRTUAL_MEMBER_METADATA_TIMEOUT_SECS` (#4508). Conda: `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MEMBER_MAX_BYTES`, `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MEMBER_MAX_DECODED_BYTES`, `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_CACHE_TTL_SECS`, `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`, `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MAX_CONCURRENT_MERGES`, `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_QUEUE_SECS` (#4555, #4608), `CONDA_ATTESTATION_ISSUERS`, `CONDA_ATTESTATION_IDENTITIES`, `CONDA_ATTESTATION_PUBLIC_KEYS` (#4556). Readiness: `READYZ_REQUIRE_SEARCH` (#4610). Rate limits: `RATE_LIMIT_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_PER_WINDOW` (#4558). Mail: `SMTP_TLS_CA_CERT`, `SMTP_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY` and `SMTP_TLS_MODE=starttls-opportunistic` (#4591). Per-repository: `virtual_metadata_partial` (#4192), `debian.flat_repository` (#4619), the conda allowlist (#4576).

**SMTP** (#4591). The transport verified the server certificate against the system trust store only, so `starttls` or `tls` against a mail server with an internal-CA certificate (common for on-premises Exchange) failed, and the only workaround was replacing the container's CA bundle. `SMTP_TLS_CA_CERT` takes a PEM path or the PEM text, and unset, the transport honours `CUSTOM_CA_CERT_PATH` like the outbound HTTP clients; the certificates are added to the system store, not substituted for it. `SMTP_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY=true` accepts any certificate and logs a warning at startup. `SMTP_TLS_MODE=starttls-opportunistic` upgrades when the server offers STARTTLS and sends in clear when it does not, the way Forgejo and Nexus behave; a STARTTLS that is offered but fails is still an error, and `starttls` still requires it. `POST /api/v1/admin/smtp/test` now answers `502` with lettre's error, what the server advertised in EHLO before and after STARTTLS (from a probe that sends no credentials, so NTLM and GSSAPI show up too) and a one-line hint, for example "set `SMTP_TLS_MODE=starttls`" for the Exchange default of NTLM in plaintext and LOGIN after STARTTLS; a bare `500` said none of that. Each delivery is bounded to 60 seconds, so a plaintext client on an implicit-TLS port no longer hangs the send.

**Quickstart and the stock compose stack** (#4313, #4478, #4479, #4480, #4481, #4482, #4555). `ADMIN_PASSWORD` applies on the first start only, and the backend now logs a warning when it is set but does not match the existing account, instead of silently ignoring it; the installer defaults to ports 30080/30443 (rootless Podman cannot publish 80), falls back to Podman when the docker CLI reaches no daemon, and says where the password is. `docker-compose.yml` ships no `JWT_SECRET` default (the backend exits once with the `openssl rand -base64 48` hint) and passes `AK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY` through only when set, so a fresh `docker compose up -d` no longer restarts the backend forever on placeholder secrets; every image name carries its registry, so podman's `short-name-mode = "enforcing"` pulls the same image as Docker; `ARTIFACT_KEEPER_VERSION` pins the openscap image too and `ARTIFACT_KEEPER_WEB_VERSION` pins the web image; only Caddy is published beyond loopback (see Security); and the Caddyfile routes `/general`, `/pacman`, `/bazel`, `/lxc` and rattler's `/t/<token>` prefix to the backend, with a CI check derived from the backend's route table so a new format cannot be left out again. Anyone who relied on reaching Postgres, OpenSearch, Trivy or OpenSCAP from another host must publish them explicitly.

Other operator-facing additions: read-only admin queues for hosted and proxy-cache quarantine holds, `GET /api/v1/admin/holds/summary` and `GET /api/v1/admin/holds/quarantine` (#4516, from #4273; scan-policy blocks appear there as active hosted holds); Kubernetes image pulls through the CI OIDC exchange with a new `kubernetes` provider type, a static JWKS for clusters the backend cannot reach, and JSON Pointer claim filters (#1246; see `docs/ci-oidc.md`); SAML login DEFLATE-encodes the AuthnRequest on the HTTP-Redirect binding, which Entra ID (`AADSTS750055`), Shibboleth and CAS require (#4475); `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS` and `SSO_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS` take effect alongside `AK_SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS` (#4428, #4474); `POST /api/v1/users/{id}/roles`, which never granted repository access, is deprecated in favour of `POST /api/v1/permissions` (#3522); a guide to Bazel module registries and how virtual repositories shadow upstream modules (#4429); maintenance and downtime banners (#2155), the guest-access runtime toggle (#867), `BLOB_GC_MIN_AGE_SECS` (#2906), LDAP group and admin re-sync on a schedule with optional deactivation (#3830), permission rules restricted by request CIDR, including anonymous read grants (#1849), and the scanner-adapter's client mode against a shared `trivy server` (#4351, adapter 1.4.0; 1.4.1 is the rebuild in #3579). The runtime images now ship `unsquashfs` for Incus SquashFS scans (#4469), and those scans now work as the image's non-root user on images with extended attributes and device nodes (#4470). The UBI image's `unsquashfs` reads gzip, xz and zstd images only; see `docs/incus-image-scanning.md`. The bundled `docker/init-dtrack.sh` grants Dependency-Track's `VIEW_POLICY_VIOLATION`; if you provisioned the Dependency-Track team yourself, grant it there too, or policy violations answer `502` (#4430). Release runs now dispatch the release announcement and the AMI build themselves (#3896, #3897).

## Other repositories

- **artifact-keeper-web:** 1.11.0 ships alongside the backend with the conda walkthrough screens and the rest of the 1.11.0 milestone (artifact-keeper-web#965), the three-state visibility control (artifact-keeper-web#840), an allowlist editor for virtual conda channels with import from a lockfile (#4576, artifact-keeper-web#971 and artifact-keeper-web#972), and severity labels that follow the backend's one definition of severity counts (#4338, artifact-keeper-web#979). Earlier items: TTL input maximum of ten years, Ed25519 key-type select, guest-access toggle and banners admin pages, project-admin membership, lifecycle assignment and composite policies, `internal` visibility, webhook `signing_mode`, and the new search and artifact fields (`last_promotion`, `format_key`, quarantine state); show a virtual repository's size from `member_storage_used_bytes` (#4423, artifact-keeper-web#958); drop the `/policy-blocks` page and the `policy_blocked` status in favour of the hold queues (#4516, artifact-keeper-web#934 and artifact-keeper-web#936); offer only the accepted webhook event names (#4419); show proxy serves in the admin download report, with a nullable `artifact_id` and the `source` filter (#4539, artifact-keeper-web#960); offer the scan-on-proxy toggle for conda, which `GET /api/v1/formats` now reports as enforced (#4585). Regenerate the SDK from the 1.11.0 spec.
- **artifact-keeper-iac (Helm chart):** values for the new settings (`GRPC_BIND_IP`, `METRICS_BIND_IP`, `BLOB_GC_MIN_AGE_SECS`, `GC_TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS`, `LDAP_SYNC_*`, `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER[_ARG]`, `SIGNING_KEY_ROTATION_OVERLAP_SECS`, `SIGNING_AUTO_MIGRATE_LEGACY_KEYS`, `CONDA_ATTESTATION_REQUIRE_VERIFIED`, `STORAGE_SCRUB_*`, the scanner-adapter `SCANNER_TRIVY_SERVER`, `S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` / `AZURE_STORAGE_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` (artifact-keeper-iac#370), and the settings listed under "New settings in this release": `UPLOAD_*`, `AK_VIRTUAL_MEMBER_METADATA_TIMEOUT_SECS`, `CONDA_VIRTUAL_*`, `CONDA_ATTESTATION_*`, `READYZ_REQUIRE_SEARCH`, `RATE_LIMIT_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_PER_WINDOW`, `SMTP_TLS_*`), scanner-adapter tag 1.4.1 (#3579), a note that the backend must be scaled to zero for this upgrade (migration 233), and, where single-flight advisory locks are enabled, `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS` below the ingress read timeout and `DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS` times replicas, plus the lock waiters, below PostgreSQL's `max_connections` (#4532). `UPLOAD_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES` defaults to half the cgroup memory limit and the conda merge budget comes out of `AK_PROXY_METADATA_BUDGET_BYTES`, so the memory request should account for both (`docs/operations/conda-virtual-merge-memory.md`). The chart must not set `AK_GUEST_ACCESS_ENABLED`, which now pins the runtime toggle.
- **artifact-keeper-cli:** lifecycle commands must send `applies_to_all: true` for a global policy (#3794); show a virtual repository's size from `member_storage_used_bytes` (#4423, artifact-keeper-cli#181); point the role-assignment command at `POST /api/v1/permissions` (#3522).
- **artifact-keeper-api:** the 1.11.0 OpenAPI spec and SDK regeneration, including the nullable `DownloadRecord.artifact_id` and the new `source` field (#4539, artifact-keeper-api#42), the promotion `gate_results` array (#4556, #4557), `components_cataloged` on proxy-scan items (#4594), the `dependencies` object on `/readyz` (#4610), the virtual conda allowlist endpoints (#4576) and `GET /api/v1/attestations/policy` (#4556).
- **walkthroughs:** the private conda channel with pixi walkthrough (`artifact-keeper.github.io/walkthroughs/private-conda-channel-pixi/`) exercises this release's conda work end to end, from a virtual channel with an allowlist and CEP-27 attestations through promotion gates to sharded solves; its scenarios are what the conda bug batches above were found against.
